newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat parliament wants peace force out in January.
newsitem.headline: Croat parliament wants peace force out in January.

text.p: Croatia's parliament demanded on Friday that U.N. peacekeepers in Eastern Slavonia, the country's last Serb-held enclave, wind up their mission when their present mandate expires in January.
The U.N. Security Council, with the final say, is widely expected to decide that more time is needed to ensure minority rights for the Serbs of Eastern Slavonia.
The U.N. has 5,000 well-armed troops in the area and along the former front line with Croatian-controlled territory.
Their purpose is to prepare the former rebel area, which has a present population of about 150,000, overwhelmingly Serb, for a peaceful return to rule from Zagreb.
But hardliners in the area have systematicaly thwarted Croatian-U.N. efforts at reintegration.
The U.N. mission began last January with a one-year mandate and an option of renewal for up to one year. U.N. officials privately envisage an extension through mid-1997.
Friday's resolution by the Croatian parliament opposed any extension and said the U.N. Transitional Authority in Eastern Slavonia should be terminated on January 15, 1997.
President Franjo Tudjman, who wants UNTAES out as soon as possible, has nevertheless held out to Western peace coordinators the possibility of a three-month extension.
Eastern Slavonia was one of three regions in Croatia seized by minority Serbs rebelling against the country's move to independence from multinational Yugoslavia in 1991.
Its present population include tens of thousands of Serb refugees from other separatist enclaves recaptured by the Croatian army in 1985.
Croat refugees from the area are meanwhile pressing the government for a swift return to their former homes and some have threatened Serbs with retribution for the events of 1991.
Ivica Kostovic, Croatia's minister for Eastern Slavonia issues, said on Friday he did not foresee a mass return of Croat refugees there until next June.
"Only when the Croatian government takes control from UNTAES will conditions be created for a mass return of refugees," Kostovic said.
In an incident on Thursday a group of Serb villagers beat up a Croatian official issuing documents in the rebel-held territory, and an UNTAES official accompanying him.
UNTAES said it had protested strongly to the local authorities and begun an investigation.
